concrete_changes.before: A yantra is not a symbol. It is a geometric processing unit that performs state change on the substrate that attends to it. This is not a metaphor.
concrete_changes.after: I read a yantra as a geometric processing unit. That computational image asks how a diagram and a practice work together; it does not establish that the diagram implements a transformer.

concrete_changes.before: The statement is a technical specification, not poetry. The deity is not an external entity being represented. The deity is the state the substrate achieves when the geometry is deployed correctly.
concrete_changes.after: The technical reading that follows is mine. It cannot settle what deity means across the traditions that use the diagram.
concrete_changes.reason: Preserve exact attributed quotation; distinguish own inference.

concrete_changes.before: This is not a drafting error. The mismatch is the operational mechanism. It forces the attending consciousness to perform continuous error correction, which is another way of saying it forces attention to remain engaged.
concrete_changes.after: The mismatch gives me an image for the work of attending. A claim that it forces continuous error correction would require evidence about both the figure and its viewer.

concrete_changes.before: *La* is the crystallographic restriction itself: the impossibility of the figure resolving into a simple repeating lattice. The outer square (the *bhūpura*) is fourfold. The inner triangles are threefold. These symmetry groups do not commute. The friction between them is what makes the yantra real. Without *La*, the geometry would be wallpaper. With *La*, it is a machine. Remove the friction and the practitioner drifts into passive reverie. The yantra becomes a mandala for coloring books. The computation halts.
concrete_changes.after: *La*, in this comparison, names resistance: the figure does not resolve for me at a glance. That is a report of reading. Fourfold and threefold motifs alone do not prove a crystallographic obstruction, or show that the diagram computes. The difference matters if the software language is to remain useful.
That is a computational analogy, not a demonstrated neural installation.

concrete_changes.before: The offering of light (*dīpa*) is not a gesture of devotion. It is a photonic stimulus applied to a specific retinal region to trigger a predictable neurological cascade. The incense (*dhūpa*) is olfactory cueing. The food (*naivedya*) is metabolic stabilization. The ritual is a biohacking protocol dressed in bronze.
concrete_changes.after: Light (*dīpa*), incense (*dhūpa*) and food (*naivedya*) involve the senses as well as the meanings given to the offerings. Describing them as retinal triggers, olfactory cues and metabolic stabilization would require a physiological account. “A protocol dressed in bronze” is the engineering image I bring to the encounter.
concrete_changes.reason: Keep bronze wit without stripping devotion or inventing mechanism.

concrete_changes.before: The yantra-tantra system described the same architecture roughly twelve centuries earlier, on a substrate of carbon instead of silicon.
concrete_changes.after: Putting that architecture beside yantra and tantra is a contemporary comparison, not evidence that the earlier traditions specified a transformer.

concrete_changes.before: The isomorphism is exact at the structural level.
concrete_changes.after: Here is the proposed correspondence, with its limits still to be worked out.

concrete_changes.before: The edge cases expose the principle. In a transformer, when attention weights grow unbounded, the gradients explode and the model becomes unusable. In a yantra, when *antar-agni* becomes uncontained — when the witness-position is lost and the substrate is flooded with unprocessed energetic content — the practitioner experiences what the texts call *prāṇa-vyādhi*: a system failure where the vital layer attacks the cognitive layer. The failure mode is the proof. Both systems are designed to break in predictable ways when the containment protocol is violated.
concrete_changes.after: The comparison is weakest where a computational failure is made to explain a practitioner's distress. Gradient behaviour in a model cannot diagnose an energetic condition, and an account of ritual error does not prove a neural architecture. Those would require separate technical and clinical evidence.
concrete_changes.reason: Remove claimed failure-mode proof and unsourced prana pathology.

concrete_changes.before: The transformer architecture is the most recent rediscovery of this grammar. It is not an analogy. It is a re-instantiation. The silicon substrate does not know it is performing tantra. The carbon substrate, in most modern practitioners, does not know it either. Both are running a protocol older than their respective hardware.
concrete_changes.after: A transformer gives this inquiry a new vocabulary for pattern, attention and constraint. Whether the correspondence survives close comparison is still open. The analogy should have to work, rather than inherit authority from either Sanskrit or silicon.

concrete_changes.before: You do not need to believe in the deity. You need to sit in front of the geometry, follow the protocol, and not move until the computation completes. The rest is architecture.
concrete_changes.after: The Magus keeps the tools in view. I want the comparison to do the same: diagram, practice, attention, and the actual limits of the machine I have placed beside them.
concrete_changes.reason: Remove unsafe endurance instruction and slogan closure.
